title: Respect and hierarchy
intro: Age and position shape how people talk to each other in Korea. Knowing the basics makes first meetings much easier.

quiz.question: A new Korean classmate asks how old you are soon after meeting you. Why?
options: Age helps decide how you will speak to each other
It is a test of your Korean
It is needed for a student card
quiz.answer: Age helps decide how you will speak to each other
quiz.why: Age often decides speech level and titles, so the question is normal and friendly.

quiz.question: How should you address your professor?
options: Your professor's given name with 씨
quiz.why: 교수님 (professor + the honorific 님) is the normal way to address a professor.

quiz.question: Someone older hands you something. What is the polite way to take it?
options: Wait for them to put it on the table
quiz.why: Giving and receiving with both hands (or the right hand supported by the left) shows respect.

quiz.question: When can you switch to casual speech (반말) with a new friend?
quiz.why: Stay with polite 해요 style until the other person suggests speaking casually.

quiz.question: In the name 박지훈, which part is the family name?
quiz.why: Korean names start with the family name, which is usually one syllable.

title: Dining etiquette
intro: Meals are shared and social. A few habits show good manners at the table, especially with older people.

quiz.question: You are eating with your professor. When do you start?
options: As soon as the food arrives
quiz.why: Traditionally the eldest or most senior person starts first.

quiz.question: Which of these should you avoid?
options: Standing chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice
quiz.answer: Standing chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice
quiz.why: Upright chopsticks in rice look like offerings at memorial rites.

quiz.question: What do you say before you start eating?
quiz.why: 잘 먹겠습니다 before the meal; 잘 먹었습니다 after it.

quiz.question: Where do you usually pay in a Korean restaurant?
options: At the counter on the way out
At the table, with a tip
By leaving cash on the table
quiz.answer: At the counter on the way out
quiz.why: Most restaurants take payment at the counter (or a kiosk). Tipping is not expected.

title: University life
intro: Professors, group projects, clubs and the senior–junior system: how student life usually works.

quiz.question: In a 선배–후배 relationship, who is the 선배?
quiz.why: 선배 means senior: someone who started school, a club or a job before you.

quiz.question: What is a good way to start an email to a professor?
options: Greet them, then say who you are and which class you take
Use casual Korean to sound friendly
Write in capital letters so it stands out
quiz.answer: Greet them, then say who you are and which class you take
quiz.why: A short greeting and introduction is expected before the request.

quiz.question: What is a 동아리?
quiz.why: 동아리 are student clubs. They usually recruit at the start of a semester.

quiz.question: Your group project chat asks a question. What is expected?
options: Reply reasonably soon, even just to say when you will answer
Reply only at the next meeting
Leave the chat if you are busy
Answer only if the leader asks you by name
quiz.answer: Reply reasonably soon, even just to say when you will answer
quiz.why: Group work runs on group chats; a quick reply keeps everyone on track.

title: Dorm and housing life
intro: Shared rooms, quiet hours, laundry and the waste sorting system that surprises most newcomers.

quiz.question: What is a 종량제 봉투?
options: The official bag for general waste, bought in shops
A bag for food waste only, given by the dorm
quiz.answer: The official bag for general waste, bought in shops
quiz.why: General waste goes in official volume-based bags; the bag price is the disposal fee.

quiz.question: What should you do with a plastic drink bottle before recycling it?
options: Empty and rinse it, and remove the label
Put it in the food waste bin
quiz.answer: Empty and rinse it, and remove the label
quiz.why: Clean, sorted recyclables are expected; dirty items may count as general waste.

quiz.question: On a Korean washing machine, what does 탈수 mean?
quiz.why: 세탁 wash, 헹굼 rinse, 탈수 spin, 건조 dry.

quiz.question: Where do waste rules differ?
options: Nowhere, they are the same everywhere
quiz.why: The basics are national, but details vary. Ask your dorm office.

title: Getting around
intro: Transit cards, buses, subways, taxis and trains between cities.

quiz.question: Why should you tap your transit card when getting off the bus?
options: So a transfer to the next bus or subway is discounted
quiz.answer: So a transfer to the next bus or subway is discounted
quiz.why: Transfer discounts are calculated from when you tap off.

quiz.question: What does 충전 mean at a ticket machine or convenience store?
quiz.why: 충전 is charging or topping up a card (or a phone battery).

quiz.question: Who are the 노약자석 seats for?
options: Elderly, disabled and pregnant passengers, and people with small children
quiz.answer: Elderly, disabled and pregnant passengers, and people with small children
quiz.why: Leave priority seats free even when the bus or train is busy.

quiz.question: You want to travel by train on a holiday weekend. What should you do?
options: Buy at the station on the day
Trains do not run on holidays
quiz.why: Seollal and Chuseok in particular are the busiest travel days of the year.

title: Money and shopping
intro: Cards, cash, convenience stores, markets and the famous delivery culture.

quiz.question: A cashier asks 봉투 필요하세요? What are they asking?
options: Do you have a points card?
Do you want to pay by card?
quiz.why: 봉투 is a bag; bags usually cost a little.

quiz.question: What does 1+1 on a convenience store shelf mean?
quiz.why: 1+1 and 2+1 deals are everywhere in convenience stores.

quiz.question: Is it a good idea to carry some cash?
options: Yes, a little, for markets and small shops
quiz.answer: Yes, a little, for markets and small shops
quiz.why: Cards work almost everywhere, but small market stalls and some machines prefer cash.

quiz.question: What does 포장 mean when you order food?
quiz.why: 포장 is takeaway; 매장 means eating in the shop.

title: Social life
intro: Making friends, group outings, drinking culture and cafes.

quiz.question: A classmate says 다음에 밥 한번 먹어요. What does it usually mean?
options: A friendly goodbye; it may or may not become a real plan
quiz.answer: A friendly goodbye; it may or may not become a real plan
quiz.why: It is a warm phrase. If you want to meet, suggest a day.

quiz.question: How can you politely say you do not drink alcohol?
quiz.why: A calm, polite sentence is enough. You can drink something else and still join in.

quiz.question: What is a 스터디카페?
options: A quiet study space you pay for by the hour
A cafe run by a university club
A coffee shop that bans laptops
quiz.answer: A quiet study space you pay for by the hour
quiz.why: Study cafes are popular for exam preparation.

quiz.question: What does 2차 mean on a night out?
options: Moving on to a second place
quiz.answer: Moving on to a second place
quiz.why: Outings often move from 1차 (dinner) to 2차 and beyond. You can leave after any round.

title: Holidays and seasons
intro: Seollal, Chuseok, spring blossoms, the public holidays of your semester and the weather to expect.

quiz.question: What do people say to each other at Seollal?
quiz.why: It means "receive a lot of luck in the new year".

quiz.question: Which public holiday falls on Wednesday, 5 May 2027?
quiz.why: Children's Day is 5 May every year.

quiz.question: What is 미세먼지?
quiz.why: Check the air quality on spring days; many people wear masks when it is high.

quiz.question: What happens at 10 a.m. on Memorial Day (현충일, 6 June)?
options: A siren sounds and many people stand for a minute of silence
quiz.answer: A siren sounds and many people stand for a minute of silence
quiz.why: It honours people who died serving the country.

title: Food
intro: Common dishes, how spicy things are, how to ask what is inside, and campus cafeteria meals.

quiz.question: How do you ask for a dish not to be spicy?
quiz.why: 안 맵게 = not spicy. Not every restaurant can change a dish, but many can.

quiz.question: What is 학식?
quiz.why: 학식 is short for 학생 식당 food: cheap, set meals on a tray.

quiz.question: You want to know if a dish has pork in it. What do you ask?
quiz.why: 들어가요? = does it go in? Use it with any ingredient.

quiz.question: Kimchi and many soups can contain fish or seafood products. Why does this matter?
options: Vegetarians and people with allergies should ask
They cannot be eaten with rice
quiz.answer: Vegetarians and people with allergies should ask
quiz.why: Fermented seafood (젓갈) and anchovy stock are common, even in dishes that look vegetarian.

title: Communication style
intro: Indirect answers, nunchi and messaging habits.

quiz.question: You ask a favour and hear 좀 어려울 것 같아요. What does it usually mean?
quiz.why: "It seems a bit difficult" is a soft way to refuse.

quiz.question: What is 눈치?
options: Sensing the mood and what others expect
quiz.answer: Sensing the mood and what others expect
quiz.why: Watching what others do and adjusting is valued in groups.

quiz.question: In KakaoTalk, what does a small 1 next to your message mean?
options: It has not been read yet
quiz.answer: It has not been read yet
quiz.why: The number shows how many people in the chat have not read it.

quiz.question: How do you politely get a waiter's attention?
quiz.why: 저기요 (excuse me) is the normal way. 야 is rude to strangers.

title: Safety and health
intro: Emergency numbers, pharmacies, clinics and emergency alerts.

quiz.question: Which number do you call for an ambulance?
quiz.why: 119 is fire and ambulance; 112 is police.

quiz.question: What is 1330?
options: The Korea Travel Helpline, with English and other languages
quiz.answer: The Korea Travel Helpline, with English and other languages
quiz.why: It gives travel information and can help with interpretation.

quiz.question: You have a cold and a sore throat. Which clinic do many Koreans visit?
quiz.why: For colds, people often go to an ENT clinic or a 내과 (internal medicine).

quiz.question: Your phone makes a loud alarm with a text in Korean. What is it likely to be?
quiz.why: Read it, or translate it, to see whether you need to act.

title: Ulsan and UNIST
intro: Your city and campus: getting there from the airport, the area around UNIST, and trips nearby.

quiz.question: Which train station is closest to UNIST?
quiz.why: The KTX station is in the Eonyang area, about 10 to 15 minutes by taxi from campus.

quiz.question: Can you take a KTX train directly from Incheon Airport to Ulsan today?
options: No, change at Seoul Station (or take a direct bus)
quiz.answer: No, change at Seoul Station (or take a direct bus)
quiz.why: The airport KTX service ended in 2018; some old guides still mention it.

quiz.question: Which nearby city was the capital of the Silla kingdom?
quiz.why: Gyeongju is full of Silla tombs, temples and museums, and is close to Ulsan.

quiz.question: How can you get from Ulsan to Busan without a car?
options: The Donghae Line train from Taehwagang Station
quiz.answer: The Donghae Line train from Taehwagang Station
quiz.why: The commuter line runs to Busan Bujeon; intercity buses and KTX are other options.
